name: Collegiate Church, Castle and Old Town of Quedlinburg
description: Quedlinburg is a small town on the northern edge of the Harz mountains in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Its streets hold around 2,100 timber-framed houses, many of them centuries old. Above them rises a castle hill crowned by the Romanesque church of St Servatius. In the 10th and 11th centuries, the town was a seat of power for the Ottonian rulers of the German Empire.
